supervisor_summary: The five revised forecasts converged tightly: fair values $79.5-82 (mean $80.7), P(close >= $76 in a year) ~58%, and thesis breaks at $58-62. They corrected every round-1 error: NTM EPS $4.58, the $2.49 dividend, the NEE-paid $4.83B fee and the October hike odds. Round-2 checks add only small facts: the Virginia SCC must rule by mid-January 2027 (~mid-March, an estimate, if the AG motion is granted) or the deal is deemed approved; the SC final order is due Jan 29 2027 with ORS testimony Oct 28; and the Uri damages remain unquantified. I keep the forecaster mean with low confidence. NEE is a rate-driven utility with ~9.8% price upside to the engine value $85.95 (record-adjusted EPS path, Kilian 2026-10-22) from $78.25 plus ~3.3% from dividends (~13.2% total), and the event calendar is heavy through Q1 2027.
key_drivers: 10-year Treasury at 5.15% (2026-10-19) vs 5.26% at the base round [24], still near post-2007 highs. NEE trades at 18.2x NTM [23]; each turn of P/E is ~$5.0/sh on the set's NTM EPS of $5.01. Whether rates ease or break higher still dominates the 12-month outcome.

Earnings compounding: Q3 adjusted EPS $1.24 vs $1.13 a year earlier, 9M $3.47 [11]. FY2026 guide $3.92-4.02 reaffirmed (high end targeted) with 8%+ CAGR off $3.71 through 2032. The set has $4.06 / $4.70 / $5.08 for FY2026-28 and NTM $5.01 at the horizon (record-adjusted guide, Kilian 2026-10-22; the pre-decision driver build had NTM $4.60). Management has beaten its first guide 4 of 4 years by a median +8.6% [13-19].
Dividend of $0.6232/qtr ($2.49/yr) growing 6% from year-end 2026 to $2.64 [11], 3.19% on the current rate and 3.38% on the FY2027 rate at $78.25 [23].

Dominion approvals: on 2026-10-19 the Virginia SCC staff recommended denial as proposed, and would not oppose approval with conditions (independent DEV board, dividend limits, jobs commitments). The governor demands a 6-year residential base-rate freeze [25]. The SCC must rule by mid-January 2027 or the deal is deemed approved [4, 30] (~mid-March 2027 if the AG clock-reset motion is granted, an estimate [3, 30]); the SC final order is expected by Jan 29 2027 [5]. NEE pays a $4.8B fee only if the deal fails on regulatory grounds [12].
Tails: the Oklahoma Uri liability ruling, where damages are unquantified and the trial is undated [7, 8]. The Florida Supreme Court appeal of FPL's 2025 rate agreement is pending [12].
